Platform designed to address growing demand for critical-mineral pricing intelligence, geopolitical supply-risk monitoring, regulatory compliance and procurement transparency

Initial focus on tungsten and antimony, with potential expansion into rare earths, semiconductors and other defense-critical materials

VisionWave intends to pursue near-term revenue opportunities through subscription-based intelligence services, compliance documentation and transaction-related services

WEST HOLLYWOOD, Calif., Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- VisionWave Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: VWAV) (“VisionWave” or the “Company”), a technology company developing advanced defense, autonomous systems and artificial intelligence solutions, today announced the acquisition of the Critical Minerals Intelligence Platform (“CMIP”), a specialized technology platform designed to provide market intelligence, supply-chain transparency, regulatory screening and procurement-related information for strategically important critical minerals.

The agreement with Litial Ltd was signed on November 18, 2026, and the acquisition has not yet closed. If completed, the acquisition would mark VisionWave's entry into the defense-industrial supply-chain intelligence market and is intended to establish a new commercial technology offering with the potential to generate recurring revenue through subscriptions, compliance-related services and transaction-based fees.

Unlike technologies requiring extensive hardware development or manufacturing infrastructure before commercialization, CMIP's software- and data-driven architecture is designed to support deployment through digital services and enterprise workflows.

According to the technology developer's materials, CMIP includes a browser-based minimum viable product (MVP) supporting benchmark monitoring, counterparty screening and compliance-document generation. VisionWave intends, following the closing of the acquisition, to evaluate these capabilities for commercial deployment and pursue initial revenue opportunities following technical, cybersecurity and regulatory validation.

The platform initially focuses on tungsten and antimony, two materials of strategic importance to defense, aerospace and advanced manufacturing. VisionWave also sees potential to extend the platform to other critical minerals, specialized industrial materials and defense-related components.

Addressing a Strategic Challenge in Defense and Industrial Supply Chains

Critical minerals have become increasingly important to national security, defense readiness, industrial resilience and international trade.

Tungsten is used in applications including aerospace components, wear-resistant materials, cutting equipment and ammunition. Antimony is used in specialized industrial and defense-related applications.

Both minerals appear on the United States' 2025 Critical Minerals List and the European Union's critical raw materials list, reflecting their economic importance and exposure to supply-chain vulnerabilities.

Global supply chains for these materials face several structural challenges:

  • Geopolitical supply concentration: Significant production and processing capacity is concentrated in a limited number of countries, creating potential exposure to geopolitical developments and trade restrictions.
  • Export controls and sanctions: International restrictions can affect material availability, supplier eligibility and cross-border transactions.
  • Pricing complexity: Market participants must navigate different material grades, delivery conditions, geographic markets and pricing methodologies.
  • Limited supply-chain visibility: Identifying the origin, processing history and chain of custody of strategically important materials can be challenging.
  • Fragmented procurement information: Pricing, counterparty verification, regulatory screening and material provenance are often handled through separate systems.

China's export restrictions on antimony-related products in 2024 and selected tungsten-related products in 2025 have further highlighted the strategic importance of supply-chain intelligence.

VisionWave believes these developments create an opportunity for technology platforms capable of combining market data, regulatory information, supplier intelligence and transaction documentation to support more informed procurement and risk-management decisions.

CMIP: An Integrated Critical Minerals Intelligence Platform

CMIP is designed as a specialized market-intelligence and workflow platform rather than simply a commodity trading application.

Its architecture brings together four complementary capabilities intended to help organizations understand critical-mineral markets, evaluate counterparties, document transactions and monitor supply-chain exposure.

1. Critical Minerals Pricing and Market Intelligence

CMIP includes a proposed benchmark pricing framework covering tungsten ammonium paratungstate (APT), antimony trioxide and antimony metal.

The framework is designed to support structured price monitoring, documented pricing methodologies and market comparisons.

By combining market pricing information with other supply-chain and transaction data, CMIP aims to support procurement planning, commercial negotiations and material sourcing decisions.

2. Regulatory Compliance and Sanctions Intelligence

The platform incorporates automated counterparty-screening workflows designed to reference relevant sanctions and restricted-party information, including U.S., European Union and United Nations sources.

Its compliance infrastructure is intended to support counterparty identity and sanctions screening, export-control information workflows, documentation of screening results and regulatory risk indicators, and compliance-related records and audit trails.

These capabilities are intended to assist compliance professionals and procurement organizations, rather than replace required legal determinations or regulatory approvals.

3. Controlled Counterparty and Transaction Network

CMIP includes a proposed closed over-the-counter network designed to connect prequalified commercial participants in strategically important materials markets.

The network architecture contemplates business-identity verification, sanctions screening, controlled participant access and structured transaction workflows.

VisionWave believes this approach could help support more transparent and accountable interactions among mineral producers, processors, traders, industrial buyers and defense-related procurement organizations.

4. Material Provenance and Supply-Chain Traceability

A central element of CMIP's long-term strategy is the development of structured data linking materials to their origins, processing history, counterparties and transaction records.

This information could enable organizations to evaluate where a critical material originated, which suppliers and intermediaries handled it, whether counterparties are subject to restrictions, and how geopolitical developments affect sourcing risks.

VisionWave believes the ability to connect material provenance, regulatory information and procurement intelligence could become an important differentiating capability as the platform develops and accumulates appropriately licensed transaction data.

Near-Term Revenue Opportunities and Commercialization Strategy

VisionWave intends to prioritize the commercialization of CMIP through three complementary revenue channels:

  • Annual subscriptions: Recurring fees for access to critical-minerals pricing intelligence, supplier-risk information, compliance tools and related services.
  • Transaction-related fees: Potential revenue from facilitating transactions through the platform's controlled counterparty network.
  • Compliance documentation services: Fees associated with screening records, documentation workflows and transaction-related compliance support.

The platform developer's proposed commercial model contemplates annual enterprise subscriptions ranging from approximately $25,000 to $75,000, transaction fees of approximately 0.25%–0.5% of matched transactions, and compliance-documentation fees of approximately $500–$2,000 per service.

These figures represent proposed pricing assumptions rather than established customer contracts or verified historical revenue. VisionWave has not independently validated these assumptions, and there can be no assurance that any customer will purchase services at these or any other prices.

VisionWave intends to pursue early commercial opportunities using the platform's existing software capabilities while evaluating additional functionality, regulatory requirements and customer needs.

The Company's objective is to establish an initial revenue-generating business and subsequently expand the platform's customer base, data coverage and integration with VisionWave's broader intelligence technologies.

Commercial deployment and the timing of any revenue generation remain subject to technical validation, customer adoption and applicable regulatory requirements.

Potential Integration with StratumAI: Toward Defense Supply-Chain Intelligence

VisionWave intends to evaluate connecting CMIP with its StratumAI intelligence architecture to develop more advanced defense supply-chain intelligence capabilities.

The proposed integration would seek to combine critical-minerals data, regulatory information, geopolitical developments and AI-supported analysis to create a more comprehensive defense-industrial intelligence capability.

Potential applications include supplier-risk monitoring, commodity price and availability intelligence, sanctioned-party detection, geopolitical supply-risk analysis, provenance review, alternative-source identification and procurement alerts.

The Company believes this approach could extend the application of AI-driven intelligence beyond physical sensing and autonomous systems into the materials and industrial supply chains that support defense technologies.

Over time, VisionWave may evaluate expanding the platform beyond tungsten and antimony to other strategically important materials and components, including rare earth elements, gallium, germanium, graphite, titanium, specialized alloys, semiconductors, electronic components and defense manufacturing inputs.

Such expansion would be subject to additional technology development, data availability, regulatory requirements and commercial validation.

Acquisition Terms and Strategic Commercial Support

Under the acquisition agreement, VisionWave has agreed to acquire CMIP from Litial Ltd for $11 million in deferred consideration, to be evidenced by an unsecured, subordinated, non-interest-bearing promissory note to be delivered at closing.

The purchase consideration is payable in two installments of $5.5 million on the first and second anniversaries of closing, subject to defined revenue milestones.

Both installments are contingent upon CMIP generating qualifying revenue of at least $500,000 during the first three months following closing and an additional $1 million during the subsequent three months. If either milestone is not achieved, both installments are forfeited. The closing of the acquisition is subject to customary conditions and to VisionWave's receipt of an independent third-party valuation of CMIP supporting the purchase price, which has not yet been delivered and which may not be waived by either party. Either party may terminate the agreement if the closing has not occurred by December 31, 2026. There can be no assurance that the valuation will support the purchase price or that the acquisition will be completed.

The acquisition is structured without an upfront cash payment or issuance of VisionWave common shares.

VisionWave also entered into a two-year strategic engagement agreement with DNE International FZ LLC to provide advisory and administrative support relating to CMIP's commercial development and operational planning.

DNE's $3.8 million contractual compensation is evidenced by a subordinated, unsecured, non-interest-bearing promissory note and is subject to the same CMIP revenue milestones and other contractual conditions, and will be cancelled if the CMIP acquisition does not close by March 31, 2027.

The Company believes the transaction structure preserves equity capital while aligning the acquisition consideration and related advisory compensation with defined commercial performance. Additional information regarding these agreements is included in the Company's Current Report on Form 8-K filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Additional Acquisition of AI-Powered Video Intelligence Technology

Separately, on November 18, 2026, VisionWave completed the $4 million acquisition of MoreSpeed, an AI-powered forensic video search technology, from SofTech Resources Limited.

MoreSpeed is designed to accelerate the identification of relevant persons, vehicles and events within large video repositories through an AI-based search and prioritization architecture.

Developer-supplied benchmarks reported median search acceleration of approximately 18.8 times against the tested baseline, which VisionWave has not independently verified and which remain subject to the Company's post-closing verification of the delivered assets.

VisionWave intends to evaluate MoreSpeed for potential integration with its existing xCalibre video analytics and broader intelligence technology portfolio.

The acquisition consideration is payable through an unsecured, non-interest-bearing promissory note due on the first anniversary of closing, subject to contractual protections. Unlike the CMIP consideration, the MoreSpeed payment obligation is not contingent on future revenue.

Management Commentary

Douglas Davis, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman of VisionWave Holdings, commented:

“Critical minerals are becoming an increasingly important component of national security, defense readiness and industrial resilience. The challenge is no longer simply obtaining these materials, but understanding where they originate, who controls their supply, how geopolitical developments affect availability, and whether procurement decisions can be supported by reliable and transparent information.

“With the planned acquisition of CMIP, we expect to enter a strategically important intelligence market that complements our broader defense technology vision.

“We believe the opportunity extends beyond conventional commodity pricing. Our objective is to bring together market intelligence, regulatory screening, supply-chain provenance and AI-supported analysis into an integrated environment that can help organizations better understand critical-material sourcing risks.

“Importantly, our near-term priority is commercialization. The platform's existing software capabilities and proposed subscription, transaction and compliance-service revenue models provide a foundation for pursuing early commercial opportunities without requiring the extensive manufacturing infrastructure associated with hardware-based products.

“CMIP also creates a potential new intelligence domain for StratumAI, allowing us to explore applications in defense procurement, supplier-risk analysis, geopolitical monitoring and strategic materials intelligence.

“We see the initial focus on tungsten and antimony as a starting point, with the longer-term potential to address a broader range of critical minerals, electronic components and industrial supply-chain dependencies.

“We have structured the acquisition without upfront cash consideration or equity issuance, with the purchase price tied to defined commercial revenue milestones.

“Our strategy is to acquire and develop differentiated intellectual property that can address meaningful operational challenges, generate commercial opportunities and create long-term value for VisionWave and its shareholders.”

About VisionWave Holdings, Inc.

VisionWave Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: VWAV) is a technology company developing dual-use unmanned systems, autonomous capabilities, and advanced sensing solutions for defense, security, and commercial applications. Its portfolio includes the VARAN unmanned ground vehicle (UGV) platform and a suite of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and drone solutions, supported by sensing, perception, and autonomy technologies. FISHERS, IN / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / American Resources Corporation (NASDAQ:AREC) ("American Resources") and ReElement Technologies Corporation ("ReElement"), a leading U.S. operator of advanced critical mineral refining and separation technologies in which American Resources maintains a strategic minority ownership interest, today announced that the Frontier Minerals Consortium ("Frontier"), of which both companies are members, has been selected by the Government of Kenya as the successful bidder in the competitive international tender for the Mrima Hill Niobium, Rare Earth Elements and Other Minerals Development Project in Kwale County, Kenya.

The selection, announced by Kenya's Ministry of Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs, represents a significant milestone in advancing one of the world's most strategically important undeveloped rare earth and niobium deposits. Frontier has been selected to enter exclusive negotiations toward a prospecting license, with subsequent activities subject to applicable regulatory approvals, community engagement and licensing requirements.

Frontier is partnered with American Resources, ReElement and Bunker Hill Silver Corp. ("Bunker Hill"), bringing together complementary expertise in mineral resource development, critical minerals supply chains and advanced refining technologies. The consortium's integrated approach is designed to support the development of a comprehensive mine-to-material value chain, emphasizing domestic processing and refining, local economic participation and long-term value creation in Kenya.

Through its Platform Orchestration model, American Resources serves as a strategic supply-chain and commercial development partner, connecting mineral resource opportunities with advanced processing and refining capabilities, including those of ReElement, and downstream markets.

As part of its participation in the consortium, American Resources expects to hold an equity interest in Frontier, subject to definitive agreements among the consortium partners. ReElement participates as the consortium's advanced refining technology partner, contributing its proprietary chromatography-based separation and purification capabilities, with the opportunity to generate refining-related revenues through future technology deployment, processing and commercial arrangements, subject to feasibility studies and definitive agreements.

The consortium is pursuing a capital-efficient development strategy that includes potential non-dilutive financing, government-supported funding and other strategic financing alternatives. Consistent with its Platform Orchestration model, American Resources expects to hold an equity interest in Frontier while minimizing direct capital requirements and actively supporting the consortium through feasibility and development. This approach is designed to create long-term economic value for American Resources and its shareholders while advancing Kenya's critical mineral development and in-country value-chain objectives, subject to definitive agreements.

A Differentiated Mine-to-Material Development Strategy

A central component of Frontier's proposal is the development of an integrated critical minerals value chain within Kenya, extending beyond traditional resource extraction and concentrate exports to include domestic mineral processing, advanced separation and refining, workforce development and downstream market integration.

The consortium's selection reflects a proposal designed to address Kenya's stated objectives for domestic mineral beneficiation, local economic participation, environmental stewardship and responsible resource development.

American Resources contributes its international resource sourcing, feedstock aggregation, strategic partnerships and critical minerals supply-chain development capabilities. ReElement contributes its proprietary, patented chromatography-based separation and refining platform, designed to produce high-purity, specification-grade rare earth elements and other critical minerals through modular, scalable processing systems. Bunker Hill contributes mining, engineering, metallurgical processing and project development expertise, providing an integrated approach to evaluating and potentially developing the Mrima Hill resource.

Together, these capabilities are intended to support the development of a commercially sustainable supply chain that retains more economic value in Kenya while expanding access to strategically important critical minerals for U.S. and allied manufacturers.

Advanced U.S. Refining Technology Supporting Kenyan Value Creation

ReElement's chromatography-based technology represents a differentiated approach to critical mineral refining, utilizing water-based separation processes designed to reduce chemical consumption, energy requirements and environmental impacts compared with conventional solvent extraction methods.

Originally developed at Purdue University and licensed in 2021, the technology has since been advanced and commercialized through ReElement's proprietary research, engineering and intellectual property development. ReElement has validated separation and purification capabilities across 15 rare earth elements and additional critical minerals, achieving purities of up to 99.999% for select products.

The company commissioned its first commercial-scale chromatography columns for germanium production at the facility in August 2026 and continues to progressively scale its domestic refining capabilities.

ReElement's proposed role in the Mrima Hill project will focus on developing optimized commercial processing and refining flowsheets utilizing its proprietary chromatography-based technology. This approach is designed to support the phased deployment of modular refining infrastructure in Kenya, enabling the production of high-purity, value-added critical mineral products within the country, subject to project-specific technical, commercial and regulatory requirements. Beyond Mrima Hill, ReElement's participation is expected to create opportunities to evaluate additional critical mineral feedstocks throughout Kenya and the broader region, with the objective of leveraging potential shared refining infrastructure, enhancing capital efficiency and technology utilization, and supporting Kenya's emergence as a regional hub for advanced critical mineral refining.

This approach is intended to support the production of higher-value refined materials within Kenya rather than limiting the country's participation to the export of raw minerals or intermediate concentrates.

A Strategic Opportunity for Kenya and the United States

Mrima Hill contains historically identified rare earth and niobium mineralization, including elements important to permanent magnets, aerospace, advanced electronics and other strategic industries. Historical mineral resource estimates indicate significant mineralization; however, these estimates have not been verified as current mineral resources and will require further technical evaluation.

The project represents an opportunity to align Kenya's economic development and industrialization objectives with the United States' strategic interest in building diversified, secure, transparent and traceable critical mineral supply chains.

By supporting domestic processing and refining, the consortium's proposed development model seeks to create opportunities for Kenyan workers, technical professionals, suppliers and local communities while establishing additional sources of high-value critical materials for international manufacturers.

Mark C. Jensen, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of American Resources Corporation, commented: "This selection represents much more than an important milestone for the Frontier Minerals Consortium. It reflects a shared vision of how critical mineral resources can be developed to create lasting economic value for resource-rich countries while strengthening the industrial and national security interests of the United States and its allies.

"For too long, many resource-rich nations have participated primarily at the extraction stage of the global minerals supply chain, while much of the downstream processing, refining and economic value has been captured elsewhere. We believe the opportunity at Mrima Hill is to help change that model by bringing together world-class mining capabilities, advanced American refining technology and integrated supply-chain development.

"Our Platform Orchestration model is designed to create meaningful economic participation in strategic resource opportunities through partnerships and equity interests, while leveraging third-party capital and minimizing direct development expenditures. We believe this approach allows American Resources to participate in globally significant projects while remaining focused on capital efficiency and the creation of long-term shareholder value.

"Importantly, this announcement is not the culmination of our efforts, but the beginning of a much broader opportunity. We look forward to working alongside the Government of Kenya, local communities and our consortium partners to advance a responsible, commercially sustainable development strategy that creates meaningful value for Kenya and strengthens critical mineral supply chains for the United States. We believe this collaborative approach can serve as a model for mutually beneficial partnerships in other resource-rich jurisdictions where we are actively developing relationships and opportunities."

Next Steps

Following the Government of Kenya's selection, Frontier intends to advance the required community engagement, regulatory and prospecting-license application processes in accordance with Kenyan law.

Subject to receipt of the necessary approvals, the consortium's proposed development program includes confirmation drilling, updated mineral resource evaluation, metallurgical test work, refining technology assessments, environmental and social studies, and preparation of a bankable feasibility study.

The feasibility process will focus on developing integrated mining, mineral processing and advanced refining flowsheets, leveraging ReElement's proprietary chromatography-based platform to support the production of high-purity, value-added critical minerals within Kenya. This approach is designed to establish a commercially viable, mine-to-material development model that maximizes in-country value-chain capture while supporting diversified critical mineral supply chains for the United States and its allies.

The consortium recognizes the environmental, cultural and social significance of Mrima Hill and intends to work with Kenyan authorities, local communities and other stakeholders to evaluate the project responsibly and in accordance with applicable requirements.

About American Resources Corporation

American Resources Corporation (NASDAQ:AREC) operates a diversified critical materials platform through its Platform Orchestration strategy, which coordinates complementary capabilities across commercial feedstock origination, resource sourcing, industrial processing and advanced refining partnerships. This capital-efficient approach enables the Company to align resources, technologies and commercial relationships to evolving customer requirements and national priorities while strengthening U.S. and allied critical mineral supply chains.

The Company's operating platforms span conventional and unconventional resource sourcing, feedstock aggregation, recycling, processing and conditioning, complemented by its strategic ownership interest in ReElement Technologies Corporation, a leading U.S. advanced materials transformation and refining company. Through these complementary capabilities and strategic relationships, American Resources seeks to connect diverse feedstock sources with advanced processing and refining solutions, enabling greater value chain capture and supporting growing commercial, industrial and defense-sector demand.

American Resources' modular, asset-light business model emphasizes disciplined capital allocation, scalable operations and strategic partnerships. By coordinating specialized capabilities across the critical materials value chain without requiring traditional vertical integration, the Company seeks to expand commercial opportunities and support resilient, economically sustainable supply chains serving infrastructure, defense, advanced manufacturing, semiconductors, energy and electrification markets.

For more information, visit americanresourcescorp.com or connect with the Company on Facebook, Twitter and LinkedIn.

About ReElement Technologies Corporation

ReElement Technologies Corporation, a strategic portfolio holding of American Resources Corporation (NASDAQ:AREC), is a leading U.S. developer and operator of advanced materials transformation and refining technologies. Its modular, refining-first platform utilizes proprietary, patented chromatography-based separation and purification technology to transform diverse feedstocks - including primary mineral concentrates, recycled materials, industrial byproducts and other unconventional sources - into high-purity, specification-grade critical materials. ReElement's flexible technology enables the co-location of advanced refining capabilities closer to feedstock sources and downstream customers, supporting greater value chain capture while reducing chemical consumption and environmental impact. The Company supports secure, resilient U.S. and allied supply chains serving defense, aerospace, semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, permanent magnets, energy and battery technologies.

For more information, visit reelementtech.com or connect with the Company on Facebook, Twitter and LinkedIn.

CINCINNATI, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- GE Aerospace (NYSE: GE) received notice of an unsolicited "mini-tender" offer by Potemkin Limited (Potemkin) to purchase up to 10,000 shares of GE Aerospace common stock, which represents less than 0.001% of the shares outstanding, at a price of $186.00 per share in cash. Potemkin’s offer price is 34.88% less than the $285.64 closing price per share of GE Aerospace’s common stock on October 23, 2026, the last trading day before the mini-tender offer commenced and is 41.67% less than the $318.88 closing price per share of GE Aerospace’s common stock on November 19, 2026, the day prior to this press release.

GE Aerospace does not endorse Potemkin’s unsolicited mini-tender offer and recommends that GE Aerospace shareholders do not tender their shares in the offer because the offer is at a price significantly below the current market price for GE Aerospace’s shares.

Shareholders should obtain current market quotations for their shares, consult with their broker or financial advisor, and exercise caution with respect to Potemkin’s mini-tender offer. GE Aerospace recommends that shareholders who have not responded to Potemkin’s offer take no action. Shareholders who have already tendered their shares may withdraw them according to Potemkin’s offering documents.

Mini-tender offers seek to acquire less than five percent of a company's outstanding shares. Consequently, they can avoid many disclosure and procedural requirements of U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) rules that apply to offers for more than five percent of a company's outstanding shares.

The SEC has cautioned investors about mini-tender offers, stating that mini-tender offers “have been increasingly used to catch investors off guard,” and that investors “may end up selling their securities at below-market prices.” The SEC's guidance to investors on mini-tender offers is available at https://www.sec.gov/reportspubs/investor-publications/investorpubsminitendhtm.html.

GE Aerospace encourages brokers and dealers, as well as other market participants, to review the SEC's letter regarding broker-dealer mini-tender offer dissemination and disclosure available at https://www.sec.gov/divisions/marketreg/minitenders/sia072401.htm.

GE Aerospace requests that a copy of this press release be included with all distributions of materials relating to Potemkin’s mini-tender offer for shares of GE Aerospace's common stock.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Review

Revenue

Total revenue in the third quarter of 2026 was $37.7 million, representing a decrease of 79.1% from $180.7 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to the decline in Cloud Mining Solutions and Mining Equipment Sales revenue.

Revenue from Cloud Mining Solutions for the third quarter of 2026 was $13.8 million, an 88.8% decrease from $122.9 million in the same period of 2025. This decline was primarily attributable to lower average selling prices, driven by lower year-over-year average BTC prices, and weaker market sentiment.

Revenue from Bitcoin self-mining operations in the third quarter of 2026 was $18.4 million, compared with $20.1 million in the same period of 2025. The year-over-year change primarily reflected the combined effect of: (1) a 38.0% decline in the average BTC price to $71,000 in the third quarter of 2026 from $114,500 in the third quarter of 2025; and (2) a 50.9% increase in average hashrate allocated to self-mining operations.

Revenue from mining equipment sales was $2.0 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $35.8 million in the same period of 2025, driven by lower customer demand amid Bitcoin price uncertainty and broader market sentiment.

Revenue from Hosting and Other was $3.5 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared with $1.9 million in the third quarter of 2025. The year-over-year increase was primarily driven by our Buy and Host one-stop solution, which continued to attract clients seeking asset ownership with simplified, hassle-free mining operations.

Cost of Revenue

Cost of revenue in the third quarter of 2026 was $39.7 million, a decrease of 77.1% from $173.5 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was mainly attributable to a reduction in scale.

Operating Income/(Expenses)

Sales and marketing expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$1.1 million, a significant increase from US$0.6 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to share-based compensation expenses of US$0.8 million, compared to less than US$0.1 million during the same period of 2025, partially offset by the absence of sales commission expenses, which amounted to US$0.2 million in the third quarter of 2025.

General and administrative expenses, and research and development expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were $2.1 million and $0.6 million, respectively. Excluding the increase in share-based compensation expenses of $0.3 million, these expenses were approximately in line with those in the same period of 2025.

Credit loss provision for other current assets was $2.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with nil in the same period of 2025. Of the $2.6 million provision, $2.05 million, representing 50% of the prepaid investment made in connection with the pending acquisition of a Bitcoin mining facility in Ethiopia, reflects the uncertainty around the transaction, as disclosed in the Company’s September 2026 operating update. The Company continues to actively pursue all available measures to protect its legal rights and financial interests, as well as those of its shareholders.

The Company recognized a $36.5 million fair value gain on digital assets and digital asset-related receivables or payables in the third quarter of 2026, reflecting the recovery in Bitcoin prices during the period. By comparison, the Company recognized a $10.0 million fair value gain in the third quarter of 2025.

Net Income

Net income in the third quarter of 2026 was $24.9 million, compared to the net income of $11.6 million in the same period of 2025.

Adjusted EBITDA

Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter of 2026 was $35.0 million, compared to $22.1 million in the same period of 2025.

Liquidity and Capital Resources

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents and digital assets of $145.3 million, compared to $177.1 million as of December 31, 2025. The decrease was primarily driven by the realization of Bitcoin holdings to fund ongoing operations and the net repayment of $11.5 million in Bitcoin-backed loans.
